absent: Workqueue pool creation, worker scheduling order, and accounting increment failure reasons beyond first inactive activation.
Security policy behind capability get and set decisions and audit record contents.
Cgroup path formatting, file operations, pidlist construction, and pressure stall handling.
Architecture stack unwinding, register handling, and bounded trace descriptor internals.
Control flow trap emission, type identifier assignment, and warning flag configuration.
Bounds header consumption and definitions of page flag, zone, and reclaim parameters.
User namespace lifecycle, reference counting, and identifier mapping tables.
Keyring change handlers and process connector event delivery.

findings.text: User space enters capability management through two system operations, one to query the effective permitted and inheritable sets for a process identifier and one to replace those sets for the caller. Query validates a versioned header, resolves the target, and returns truncated halves when an older layout is requested. Update restricts effects to the caller and applies them through a credential transaction.

A self test entry exercises stack reporting from normal process context, from deferred work context, and from a saved address array path, bracketed by informational messages. The deferred path enqueues a work item on a system queue and waits for completion. One build variant skips the saved path.

Stack helpers are available to other kernel parts: one routine prints a stored address array with indentation, and two build variants capture the current call chain into a caller buffer while skipping a requested number of recent frames plus the capture frame itself, returning how many addresses were stored.

Process lookup helpers resolve a virtual identifier in the active namespace of the caller, then map the internal pid object to its thread group leader. The namespace lookup delegates to an identifier table search.

Credential management exposes operations to duplicate the current security context for modification, to publish a prepared context with side effects, and to discard a prepared context without publishing. Duplication and publication handle reference counts and notifications.

Capability query helpers let callers test whether a task holds a capability in a given user namespace, with variants that suppress auditing or mark set identity context, plus convenience forms for the initial namespace, for file credentials with validity checking, for inode mapping with namespace privilege, and for a tracer credential where absence means no extra restriction.

Control flow integrity support exposes failure reporting that distinguishes warning from fatal handling, a predicate that recognises trap addresses in the core table or in module tables, finalisation that locates a module trap section by name, plus helpers to set dumpability on the current execution state and to transfer active references between user namespaces during credential change.

Filesystem setup state for the grouping subsystem embeds generic kernfs setup state and adds a root reference, a namespace reference, option flags, toggles for cloning behaviour and empty or full selection, a bitmask of chosen subsystems, and owned strings for hierarchy name and release notification path. A converter recovers the enclosing record from the embedded generic part.

Per open file state for grouping control files keeps a namespace reference together with separate small groups for pressure trigger data, process iteration progress, legacy process list caching, and peak tracking. The process group records whether iteration started and carries an iterator; the legacy group caches a process identifier list.
Trace path scratch length is 1024 bytes.

A host build tool emits numeric limits for page flags, zones, spinlock size, processor bit width on symmetric builds, and generational reclaim widths, with zero fallbacks when that reclaim option is off. Two preprocessor markers indicate bounds header generation mode.

Node concurrency limit updates require the queue mutex to be held and operate on the effective mask of the unbound pool. Unbound queue selection dereferences either a per processor slot or a default slot and asserts that one of the global pool mutex or the queue mutex is held.

Task resolution and several capability and tracer checks execute under read side critical sections, releasing before returning. Execution state and tracer credential accesses use protected dereference, and module address lookup for trap checks runs under a scoped guard.
Grouped tracing of a path string serialises formatting and emission with a spin lock that saves interrupt state, using a shared scratch buffer whose length matches the stated constant.

Header validation reads a version field from user space. The oldest version triggers a one time legacy warning and requests one word per set; the middle version triggers a one time deprecation warning and shares handling with the newest version requesting two words per set. Any other version causes the current kernel version to be written back when possible and an invalid argument result.

Capability query rejects negative identifiers and missing targets, otherwise obtains three sets from the security layer. It presents each wide set as low then high halves and copies only as many words as the negotiated version allows, silently dropping upper bits for older callers. A null data pointer with a version mismatch probes support without failing.

Capability update only affects the caller and rejects other identifiers. It bounds the user copy to a small fixed array, combines low and high halves under a validity mask, prepares new credentials, delegates the policy decision, records an audit event on success, then publishes or discards the prepared credentials according to the policy result.

Per node concurrency limits share a global maximum in proportion to online processors in the effective mask that belong to each node, with an optional excluded processor removed from totals. Each share is rounded up then clamped between a configured minimum and the global maximum. When no processor remains, nodes fall back to the minimum and the non uniform case keeps the full maximum.

Activation takes the oldest inactive item when accounting permits and moves it plus any following linked companions to the pool execution list in order, clearing the inactive mark and refreshing a progress timestamp when the destination was empty. Traversal callers can receive an updated cursor when multiple items move during a safe walk.

Publishing credentials compares identity and capability subset relations to decide dumpability, clears pending death notification on change with an ordering barrier, updates keyring associations on filesystem identity change, adjusts process count accounting when user or namespace changes, publishes both credential pointers, transfers namespace activity, emits identifier change notifications, and releases the old references.

Preparing credentials allocates a new record, copies the current contents, resets non reference counted state, takes references on group, user, namespace and usage counters, retains keyrings and usage counts where configured, and invokes a security preparation hook. Any allocation or hook failure discards the partially built record and reports absence.

Stack capture variants accept a caller buffer, its capacity, and a skip count. Both add one to skip their own frame, walk the current thread, and return the number of addresses stored. One variant uses a consume callback with explicit cookie state; the other fills a bounded trace descriptor.

Deferred context testing logs explanatory messages, schedules a stack dump work item on a dedicated system queue, and blocks until that item completes, ensuring the dump executes outside normal process context.

File based checks reject out of range capability numbers and otherwise defer to the security layer with the file credential. Inode related checks additionally require that the current namespace maps both the owning user and group identifiers of the target, with a combined helper requiring both the namespace capability and the mapping.

Trap recognition computes each candidate address as a base plus a signed offset and linearly scans a bounded table. Core tables are checked first, then the owning module table when address lookup finds one. Finalisation clears module trap bounds then records the section whose name matches the expected trap section, stopping at the first match.

Capability subset comparison in the same user namespace reduces to a set inclusion test on permitted sets. Across namespaces it succeeds only when the candidate set namespace is an ancestor of the other and the ancestor owner matches the effective user at the parent link, walking toward the initial namespace.

A logging prefix prepends the module name to capability messages. A boot time toggle can disable file based capabilities from its default enabled state, with one time warnings for legacy and deprecated caller patterns. A debug helper for credentials is compiled to no output but preserves formatting checks.
Normal context testing logs that the following trace is intentional then dumps the stack. The module exit hook performs no action.

A work item rests inactive on a per queue list, becomes eligible when accounting allows, then joins the pool execution list with its linked companions and loses the inactive mark. The pool timestamp advances only on transitions from an empty execution list.

Credential updates move from current to prepared to either published or discarded. Preparation copies and references; publication makes the new record visible on both pointers and releases the old; discard releases the prepared record without publication.

Failure handling logs the fault address and, when available, the intended target and expected type. A warning configuration emits a warning and continues with a warning outcome; otherwise the outcome is fatal.

Several defensive checks guard misuse: printing with no buffer warns and returns, credential publication and discard assert positive usage and consistent current state, dumpability values beyond the privileged level are clamped with a one time warning and shared execution state for memoryless tasks is never mutated, and invalid capability numbers warn once and fail closed.

Pid namespace lookup warns when called without read side protection. Node limit computation treats an excluded processor outside the effective mask as no exclusion and guards against an empty total through an explicit fallback path.
